rw-071.q: We keep a 'Tenant' custom object with fields Customer_Email, Assignee, Tag, and Tag_2. On any incoming reply (from anyone): if the From address or the To address is present in the Customer_Email field of a Tenant record, assign the conversation to that record's Assignee, apply the record's Tag and Tag_2, and set the status to Open.
rw-071.notes: Custom-object-driven dynamic routing (Elite). Assignee/tags are dynamic lookups into the matched Tenant record, not fixed values.

rw-072.q: On every new incoming email, call our 'get_thread_id' HTTP connector and then add a note reading 'Thread ID: {{get_thread_id.gmail_thread_id}}'.
rw-072.notes: No conditions — unconditional connector call + templated note using the connector's output variable.

rw-073.q: For each new incoming conversation, run the 'get_gmail_thread_id' HTTP request and drop the result into a note: 'Thread ID - {{get_gmail_thread_id.gmail_thread_id}}'.

rw-074.q: Carrier fraud screening: our email-verification API returns a result category per sender. When 'obtain_email_verification_result.email_search_result_category' contains any of [[g0.c0]], run the follow-up HTTP request and tag the conversation 'FRAUD'.

rw-075.q: When an email arrives with the exact subject 'TEST - Please do not delete or assign thank you!', assign it to Marco and fire our HTTP connector request.

rw-077.q: Sender verification on the Reply-To address: first check that the verification API returned a domain for 'obtain_email_verification_results_reply_to.email_domain'; then, if its result category contains 'email_and_email_domain_not_known' or 'email_domain_spoofing_attempt', run the follow-up HTTP request and tag the conversation 'Suspicious Sender'.
